verdict: Caution: lend selectively to integrated, low-leverage Bhilwara weavers/processors with verified export order books; avoid pure grey-fabric converters and leveraged capex plays until Rajasthan demand signals recover.
title: Bhilwara MMF/Polyester Weaving & Processing: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
**The sector is fixed-capital and working-capital heavy, so funding needs are high and leverage tolerance is low** [8][9]. Yarn price swings hit inventory value before they hit the P&L, so when a proposal lands, check whether yarn inventory is hedged or backed by a firm order; if it is speculative stock, ask for the buyer PO behind it. ## What has changed now
**Local news is mixed and partly dated.** A July 2026 report says West Asia conflict stalled Bhilwara export orders worth around Rs 800 to Rs 1,000 crore [2]; a June 2026 report says over Rs 3,000 crore of investment is still flowing in despite the global slump [3]. **The official data pack is the sobering part: Rajasthan GST collections are -4.7% Apr-to-date against India +6.1%, and state electricity demand is +4.0% versus India +9.5%** [D] — both point to weaker local activity than the national IIP print of +13.1% for NIC 13 [D]. **So treat Bhilwara demand as lagging the national textile upcycle; do not underwrite on the India IIP number alone.**

## Where the growth is
**Pursue integrated units that spin-or-buy yarn, weave, and process in-house, with a named export buyer list and low leverage.** Peer commentary points to MMF runway: India's per-capita fibre consumption is 5.5 kg against a global average of 11 kg, and MMF share is 56% versus 69% globally [7]. **Filatex's Q3FY26 read-across shows stable performance for value-added polyester yarn players** [4]. ## How to grow safely
**Structure for the working-capital cycle, not the capex story.** Take monthly stock-and-debtor statements, yarn purchase invoices, and buyer-wise sales; covenant on total outside liabilities to tangible net worth and on drawing power against verified receivables. **Rating methodology flags that longer-tenure term debt comfortably improves coverage** [10], so match any capex loan tenure to the asset, and confirm TUFS-style subsidy timelines before sanction [10]. **Peer guidance has already been cut to about 10% growth from an earlier 20%** [6] — so build projections on 10%, not 20%; if the borrower's numbers assume more, ask for the order book that justifies it. **Crude-linked yarn price volatility remains the key monitorable for polyester players** [11]; a sharp yarn spike with flat fabric prices means margin squeeze — ask for the last three months' yarn-to-fabric spread.
